engine_label: Claude (Sonnet) via claude -p, web search on
question: What public data sources show apartment construction permits in Texas?
answer:
Here's a rundown of where you can pull apartment/multifamily construction permit data for Texas, from broadest to most granular:

**National/state level**
- **U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)** — the standard baseline. Reports new privately-owned residential construction by state, metro, and county, broken out by units-in-structure (so you can isolate 5+ unit / apartment permits). Monthly and annual releases.
- **NAHB (National Association of Home Builders)** — republishes and visualizes Census BPS data by state and metro, useful if you want ranked comparisons across Texas metros without pulling raw Census files yourself.
- **Texas Real Estate Research Center (TRERC), Texas A&M University** — takes the Census BPS data and adds a custom query builder/"Advanced City Search" that lets you drill down below the county level for Texas specifically — probably the easiest state-focused starting point.
- **Texas Open Data Portal (data.texas.gov)** — statewide open data catalog; worth checking for any state-level permitting or construction datasets, though most granular permit data actually lives at the city level (below).

**City-level open data portals (most granular, permit-by-permit)**
- **City of Austin Open Data Portal** — has dedicated datasets like "Issued Construction Permits" and "Currently Active Commercial Multifamily Construction Permits," which is about as close to purpose-built for your question as it gets.
- **Dallas OpenData** — "Building Permits" dataset, queryable via Socrata/OData.
- **Open Data SA (City of San Antonio)** — "Building Permits" dataset from the Development Services Department.
- **Houston** — doesn't have as clean a Socrata-style portal as the above; permit data runs through the Houston Permitting Center (iPermits system). It's public but typically requires querying their permitting system directly rather than a downloadable open dataset.
- **Fort Worth, El Paso, and other metros** — check each city's own open data or development-services site; coverage and granularity vary a lot city to city.

**Commercial aggregators (not free, but worth knowing about)**
If you need permit data normalized/cleaned across many Texas cities at once (rather than stitching together each city's portal), companies like **BuildFax**, **PermitVector**, **Buildchek**, **Zonda** (formerly Metrostudy — strong for multifamily/apartment pipeline specifically), **Yardi Matrix**, **CoStar**, and **Dodge Construction Network** aggregate permit and construction-starts data, including Texas apartment projects, but these are paid products, not public sources.

For a research project, I'd start with **TRERC's building permits tool** for state/metro trend data, then go to the individual **city open data portals** (Austin, Dallas, San Antonio) for permit-level detail, and treat Houston as the odd one out requiring direct queries to its permitting system.

Sources:
- [Building Permits by State and Metro Area | NAHB](https://www.nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/state-and-local-data/building-permits-by-state-and-metro-area)
- [Building Permits | Texas Real Estate Research Center](https://trerc.tamu.edu/data/building-permits/)
- [Currently Active Commercial Multifamily Construction Permits | City of Austin Open Data](https://data.austintexas.gov/Building-and-Development/Currently-Active-Commercial-Multifamily-Constructi/hah9-7x5p)
- [Issued Construction Permits | City of Austin Open Data](https://data.austintexas.gov/Building-and-Development/Issued-Construction-Permits/3syk-w9eu)
- [Building Permits | Dallas OpenData](https://www.dallasopendata.com/Services/Building-Permits/e7gq-4sah)
- [Building Permits | Open Data SA - City of San Antonio](https://data.sanantonio.gov/dataset/building-permits)
- [State of Texas Open Data Portal](https://data.texas.gov/)
